topic: Move Semantics and Rvalue References Distinguishing Lvalues
explanation: In modern C++, move semantics enable efficient transfer of resources from temporary objects (rvalues) to new objects, reducing unnecessary copying and improving performance. Rvalue references (denoted by &&) are a key feature that allow functions and constructors to distinguish between lvalues and rvalues, facilitating move semantics. This is especially important in resource-managing classes, such as containers and smart pointers, to optimize resource transfer without expensive copying.
